Description: Whether the reported variable is an individual result or combines several, and if combined, how: the statistical model used, including any criteria governing which model is applied, and what the individual results are combined over (for example per grain, per phase within a sample, or per sample). Record 'Not combined' where each individual result is reported on its own. Record the model only; the software implementing it belongs in Data Processing Software. In the dataset: report each combined value with its uncertainty and the number of individual results it combines, and identify, for each individual result, the combined value it contributes to.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., Arithmetic mean per phase within each sample | Weighted mean with MSWD-based uncertainty expansion | York (1969) isochron regression | Not combined
Purpose: A methodological choice that changes the result: an arithmetic and a weighted mean of the same data, or a Model-1 and a Model-3 regression, give different values and different uncertainties.

Description: The rules determining which individual results contribute to a combined result: the limits a result must meet (for example on analytical total or stoichiometry) and the grounds on which one is rejected (for example overlap onto a neighbouring phase, or an outlier test with its threshold), including any acceptance threshold on the dispersion statistic. An individual result is the value of the reported quantity obtained from one acquisition: a replicate measurement of the same solution or location, a spot or grain within a sample, or an independently prepared aliquot or digestion, whichever the procedure combines. Distinct from filtering the acquired signal during data reduction (removing spikes, cycles or scans, or discarding an acquisition whose signal is compromised): this field records the rules by which finished results enter a combined result. In the dataset: flag each individual result excluded from a combined value, with the rule that excluded it.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'Totals 98.5–101.5 wt%; points overlapping a neighbouring phase rejected' | 'All results included; no filter applied'
Purpose: The same measurements give different combined values under different acceptance rules, so the rules are needed to reproduce a combined value from its individual results.

Description: The statistic used to describe the scatter among the individual results contributing to a combined value, or to test whether that scatter exceeds what analytical uncertainty alone predicts: for example one standard deviation of the mean, or the MSWD with its probability of fit. A threshold for accepting it belongs with the inclusion criteria. In the dataset: report, for each combined value, the value of the statistic, and any further statistic (for example the standard error of the mean, or a 95% confidence interval) beside it, named.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., One standard deviation of the mean | MSWD with probability of fit
Purpose: Without the statistic named, the uncertainty given with a combined value cannot be interpreted, nor can whether the combined results form a single population be judged.
